gear.name: Canon EOS R8
gear.details: 24.2MP full-frame. No in-body stabilization — only lens IS. No full mechanical shutter (electronic first-curtain or electronic). LP-E17 battery: short life, carry spares. E3 wired-remote socket. Built-in Interval timer, Bulb timer and Time-lapse movie.

gear.name: Laowa 15mm f/2 Zero-D
gear.details: RF mount, manual focus and manual aperture ring, no electronic contacts. Needs Release shutter w/o lens: Enable. Near-zero distortion, 110° view. No EXIF lens data.

gear.name: Canon RF 24-50mm f/4.5-6.3 IS STM
gear.details: Compact kit zoom with optical IS. No filters in kit fit 58mm.

gear.name: Canon RF-S 55-210mm f/5-7.1 IS STM
gear.details: APS-C lens: R8 auto-crops to ~10MP, 88–336mm equivalent. Optical IS.

gear.name: Canon RF 100-400mm f/5.6-8 IS USM
gear.details: Optical IS, fast Nano USM AF. Main lens for moon, aircraft and wildlife.

gear.name: Samyang 135mm f/2 (SY135M-C)
gear.details: EF mount, manual focus, manual aperture, no electronic contacts. Mounts through the Drop-in Filter Adapter. Needs Release shutter w/o lens: Enable. No stabilization.

gear.name: UV filter 55mm
gear.details: Protection only. Remove at night to avoid ghosting.

gear.name: Circular polarizer 55mm
gear.details: Cuts glare and haze, deepens blue sky. Costs ~1.5 stops.

gear.name: FLD filter 55mm
gear.details: Corrects green fluorescent cast. Rarely needed shooting RAW.

gear.name: NiSi True Color CPL 67mm
gear.details: Neutral polarizer for the RF 100-400. Cuts atmospheric haze at long focal lengths. Costs ~1.5 stops.

gear.name: K&F Variable ND (ND4–ND64) + CPL 72mm
gear.details: 2–6 stops variable ND with built-in polarizer. Near the max end it can show a dark X on the 15mm — back off a little.

gear.name: NEEWER ND1000 10-stop 72mm
gear.details: 10 stops: multiply metered time by ~1000 (1/30 s → 30 s). Expect a slight color cast; fix WB in RAW.

gear.name: NiSi Natural Night 72mm
gear.details: Light-pollution filter. Cuts orange sodium street-light glow; slight cool cast.

gear.name: Canon Drop-in Filter Mount Adapter EF-EOS R
gear.details: EF→RF adapter with filter slot. Required for the Samyang 135. Keep a drop-in filter (Clear A if nothing else) in the slot.

gear.name: Drop-in Circular Polarizing Filter A
gear.details: Polarizer for EF lenses on the adapter. Rotate with the thumbwheel on the filter.

gear.name: Drop-in Clear Filter A
gear.details: Default insert for the adapter when no other drop-in filter is used.

gear.name: Drop-in astro light-pollution filter
gear.details: Cuts sodium/mercury light pollution on EF lenses through the adapter.

gear.name: INNOREL RT75C carbon tripod
gear.details: Carbon legs, no head. Hang your bag from the hook in wind.

gear.name: INNOREL ER362C center column extension
gear.details: Extra height. Raising the column adds shake — avoid for long exposures and 400mm.

gear.name: Leofoto LH-40 ball head
gear.details: Low-profile ball head, Arca quick release.

gear.name: Wired intervalometer (E3)
gear.details: Plugs into the R8 remote socket. Delay, long-exposure (bulb), interval and frame count.

guides.title: Ocean & Landscape
guides.summary: Daytime coast and scenery, sharp front to back

settings.label: Focus
settings.value: One Shot, 1 point ⅓ into scene · Laowa: MF ~1 m at f/8

gear.note: Laowa: use the CPL ring, ND at minimum

steps: Mount the lens. Laowa: enable Release shutter w/o lens.
Av, f/8, ISO 100, Daylight WB, RAW.
Fit the polarizer and rotate it until glare on water and foliage drops.
Focus ⅓ into the scene (Laowa: set ~1 m on the scale at f/8 — sharp from ~0.5 m to infinity).
Level the horizon with the electronic level (INFO button).
Check the histogram and highlight alert; pull exposure comp down until whites stop blinking.
High contrast? Use AEB 3 frames ±2 EV on the tripod and blend later.
tips: Best light: first and last hour of sun.
Put a rock, tide pool or driftwood in the bottom third.
f/16+ softens the image from diffraction — stay at f/8–f/11.
warnings: A polarizer on the 15mm darkens the sky unevenly — rotate to minimum or remove it when the sky fills the frame.
Highlight Tone Priority (D+) raises the minimum ISO to 200 — leave it off and bracket instead.
Laowa 15 has no contacts: without Release shutter w/o lens the shutter will not fire.

guides.title: Night Street
guides.summary: City scenes at night or late evening, handheld

settings.label: Aperture
settings.value: f/2 – f/4 primes · wide open on 24-50

settings.label: Focus
settings.value: Servo + Eye detect (24-50) · MF zone ~3 m at f/4 (primes)

settings.label: Exp. comp
settings.value: −⅔ EV to keep the night mood

gear.note: f/2 candids from across the street

steps: Remove screw-on UV/protective filters — they cause ghosting from street lights.
Set Shutter mode to Electronic 1st-curtain.
Av, widest practical aperture, Auto ISO max 12800 with a minimum shutter speed set in Auto ISO.
24-50: Servo AF, subject People, Eye detection on.
Primes: MF, focus peaking on, pre-focus ~3 m at f/4 and shoot from the hip.
Exposure comp −⅔ EV so lights don't blow out and shadows stay dark.
tips: Wet pavement doubles the light — shoot after rain.
Stand still near a lit shop window and let people walk into the light.
Blue hour (20–40 min after sunset) balances sky and street lights.
warnings: Electronic shutter shows banding under LED and sodium lights — use Electronic 1st-curtain.
R8 has no IBIS: the Laowa 15 and Samyang 135 are unstabilized — stay ≥ 1/30 at 15mm and ≥ 1/250 at 135mm.
Laowa and Samyang have no contacts: enable Release shutter w/o lens.

guides.title: Moon

settings.label: Focus
settings.value: MF, 10× magnified on the shadow line

steps: Tripod low and solid; center column down.
Lens at 400mm, IS off (lens switch or the camera's IS menu), focus to MF.
M mode, f/8, 1/250, ISO 200 as a starting point.
Magnify 10× on the terminator (shadow edge) and focus until craters are crisp.
Check the histogram: the moon's brightest part should sit just left of the right edge.
Fire with the 2-s timer or intervalometer; take 20–50 frames to stack later.
tips: Half moon shows more crater detail than full moon.
Shoot when the moon is high — low moons are blurred by atmosphere.
Include a landscape? Shoot a moonrise at dusk when sky and land are both lit.
warnings: Evaluative metering overexposes the moon against a black sky — use M.
Turn IS off on the tripod — at 400mm it can drift.
The ER362C extension adds shake at 400mm — leave it off.

guides.title: Ferry Night Time-lapse
guides.summary: Ferry crossing at night as a time-lapse

settings.label: Shutter
settings.value: 2 – 4 s for light trails on water

settings.label: Focus
settings.value: AF on far lights, then switch to MF

settings.label: Metering
settings.value: Evaluative to set, then lock in M

settings.label: Frames
settings.value: 240 = 10 s clip at 24 fps (5 s interval ≈ 20 min)

steps: Arrive before the ferry; tripod out of foot traffic, bag hung for weight.
Compose with space for the ferry's path.
M mode, f/8, 3 s, ISO 200; adjust ISO until the histogram looks right.
Manual WB ~3800K; Long exposure NR Off; Wi-Fi and Bluetooth off.
Focus on distant lights with AF, then flip to MF so it can't refocus.
Interval 4–5 s (shutter + 1–2 s), frames 240+; start the interval timer or intervalometer.
Don't touch the tripod until it finishes.
tips: Shutter of 2–4 s turns ferry lights into streaks while keeping the hull recognizable.
In-camera Time-lapse movie gives a ready 4K clip but no RAW frames.
Start in blue hour and let it run into darkness for a day-to-night transition (use Av with care, or adjust ISO between frames in small steps).
warnings: Long exposure noise reduction doubles each frame's time and leaves gaps — turn it Off.
Auto WB, Auto ISO or Av cause flicker between frames — lock everything in M.
An active Wi-Fi/Bluetooth connection can block the built-in interval timer — turn them off or use the wired intervalometer.
LP-E17 batteries run down fast on long sequences — start with a full one.

guides.title: Star Trails

settings.label: Focus
settings.value: MF on a bright star at 10×, then tape the ring

settings.label: Drive
settings.value: Wired: 30 s exp + 1 s gap · Built-in timer: 31–32 s interval · 120–240 frames

steps: Enable Release shutter w/o lens. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth off.
Point north at Polaris for circles, or east/west for straight lines; include a foreground.
M mode, f/2.8, 30 s, ISO 1600, WB 4000K, Long exp. NR Off.
Magnify 10× on a bright star; turn the focus ring until it's smallest. Tape the ring.
Take a test shot and check the histogram; adjust ISO.
Wired intervalometer: 30 s exposure, 1 s gap. Built-in Interval timer: interval is start-to-start, so set 31–32 s. 120–240 frames (1–2 hrs).
At the end, take 10 dark frames with the lens cap on, same settings.
Stack in StarStaX or Sequator.
tips: New moon gives the darkest sky; a quarter moon lights the foreground nicely.
A brief headlamp sweep over the foreground in one frame adds detail.
Plane trails can be removed during stacking.
warnings: Long exposure noise reduction doubles each frame and leaves gaps in the trails — must be Off.
Dew fogs the front element over hours — check every 20–30 min.
LP-E17 may not last 2 hours, especially in cold — use a USB-C PD power bank if yours supports camera power, or swap between sequences.
Laowa 15 has no contacts: enable Release shutter w/o lens.

guides.title: Waterfall Long Exposure
guides.summary: Silky water in daylight with ND

settings.label: Focus
settings.value: MF ~1 m on scale (Laowa) · AF on rocks then MF

settings.label: Metering
settings.value: Evaluative · watch highlights on white water

gear.note: ND + glare cut on wet rocks

steps: Set up the tripod low and stable; spike legs between rocks.
Compose and focus first without the filter.
Attach the K&F; rotate the CPL ring to remove glare from wet rocks and leaves.
M, f/8, ISO 100; turn the ND ring until the shutter reaches ½–2 s at a good histogram.
Fire with the 2-s timer; shoot ¼, ½, 1, 2 s and compare.
Wipe spray off the filter between frames.
tips: Overcast days are best — no harsh sun on white water.
Leaves or rocks in the foreground add depth.
Too much blur (>4 s) turns falls into fog — ½–2 s keeps structure.
warnings: Near maximum, the variable ND can make a dark X across the 15mm frame — back off a stop.
Spray droplets on the filter show as blurry spots — check each frame zoomed in.
Laowa 15 has no contacts: enable Release shutter w/o lens.

guides.title: Ocean Long Exposure
guides.summary: Glassy sea and streaky clouds with the 10-stop ND

settings.label: Focus
settings.value: Focus before fitting ND, then MF

steps: Tripod down firmly, above the surge line.
Compose, set focus (MF ~1 m at f/11), all before the filter.
M, f/11, ISO 100: meter without the filter — e.g. 1/30 s.
Screw on the ND1000 carefully without bumping focus.
Set Bulb; set the Bulb timer (or intervalometer) to metered time × 1000 — 1/30 → 30 s.
Fire with a 2-s delay; review the histogram and adjust time.
tips: Clouds moving toward or away from you streak best.
Rocks or a pier give the smooth water a solid anchor.
Exposures over ~2 min: Long exp. NR doubles the wait — plan for it.
warnings: With the ND1000 on, the EVF goes dark and AF hunts — focus and compose first.
Salt spray softens images — wipe the filter and shoot from upwind.
Rising tide sinks and shakes tripod legs — reset between frames.

guides.title: Low-flying Airplanes

settings.label: Focus
settings.value: Servo · Subject: Vehicles · Tracking on · Whole area

steps: Stand with the sun behind you along the approach path.
Tv 1/1600 for jets, 1/160 for props; Auto ISO.
Servo AF, subject Vehicles, Tracking on, Whole-area AF.
Shutter mode Electronic 1st-curtain; High-speed continuous.
Exposure comp +⅔ EV; check the plane isn't a silhouette.
Start tracking early; pan smoothly and keep panning after the burst.
tips: Props: slow shutter shows a full propeller disc — 1/125 at 100mm, 1/250 at 400mm.
Landing lights on approach make great head-on shots.
Heat shimmer over runways: shoot from a lower angle or earlier in the day.
warnings: Electronic shutter (40 fps) bends propellers and fuselages while panning — use Electronic 1st-curtain.
Pre-shooting / RAW burst only works with the electronic shutter — fine for jets head-on, not for props.
Bright sky fools the meter into dark planes — add +⅔ to +1 EV.

guides.title: Wildlife & Birds
guides.summary: Daytime wildlife in sun or under cloud

settings.label: Focus
settings.value: Servo · Subject: Animals · Eye detect · Tracking

gear.note: In the adapter for water glare

steps: Sun behind you; get low to the subject's eye level.
M mode, wide open, shutter per subject, Auto ISO with exposure comp.
Servo AF, subject Animals, Eye detection on, Tracking on.
Perched: Electronic shutter for silent 40 fps. Flight: switch to Electronic 1st-curtain.
Watch the highlight alert on white feathers; adjust exposure comp.
Short bursts; keep both eyes open to follow the subject.
tips: Overcast light is softer for feathers and fur — raise Auto ISO max.
Leave space in front of the subject's eyes in the frame.
Silent electronic shutter keeps wary animals from flushing.
warnings: Electronic shutter warps fast wingbeats — use Electronic 1st-curtain for flight.
White birds in sun blow out — dial −⅔ EV and watch the highlight alert.
No IBIS: the Samyang 135 is unstabilized — keep ≥ 1/500 and enable Release shutter w/o lens.

guides.title: Sunset

settings.label: Aperture
settings.value: f/8 – f/11 · f/16 for a sunstar (Laowa)

settings.label: Shutter
settings.value: Auto · tripod ⅛ – 2 s after sundown

settings.label: Focus
settings.value: One Shot ⅓ into scene · Laowa MF ~1 m

settings.label: Metering
settings.value: Evaluative, metered on sky beside the sun

settings.label: Timing
settings.value: Golden hour 60 min before · afterglow 10–30 min after

gear.note: Wide sky + foreground; f/16 for a sunstar
Laowa: ND to smooth water; polarizer at minimum near the sun
Big sun on the horizon at 400mm

steps: Check sunset time and direction; arrive 45 min early.
Tripod up; compose a silhouette or water reflection with the horizon on a third.
Av, f/8, ISO 100, Daylight WB, RAW, exposure comp −⅔ EV.
Meter on the sky beside the sun, not on the sun itself.
Check the highlight alert — only the sun should blink.
AEB 3 frames ±2 EV with the 2-s timer for blending later.
Keep shooting 10–30 min after sunset; switch to M and lengthen the shutter as the light fades.
tips: Mid-height clouds light up best after the sun drops — don't leave early.
Sunstar: Laowa 15 at f/16 with the sun partly hidden by the horizon or a tree edge.
Big sun: 400mm as it touches the horizon; a person, boat or tree in front adds scale.
warnings: At 400mm, only aim at the sun when it's low and orange at the horizon — a bright sun through a long lens can damage the sensor.
Auto WB neutralizes the warm colors — set Daylight or Cloudy.
A polarizer does little toward the sun and makes the 15mm sky uneven — set it to minimum or remove it.
Laowa 15 has no contacts: enable Release shutter w/o lens.
